about: Quiz of the Answer Prompt Choice lesson. a = index of the right option (0-based). Answer key: B A C A (as letters).

questions.q: Why did P0's abstain rule fit derivation exercises badly?
o: The final result of a derivation is never written in a passage, so 'the passages do not contain the answer' is almost always true.
The model could not read citation markers.
questions.f: A proof or derivation is built from facts; its result is not printed in the course text. P1 and P2 ask instead whether a needed fact is missing.

questions.q: What did the selector use to choose among the prompts?
o: Abstention when gold evidence is in the context (A_present), after a citation-validity check (CV ≥ 0.90).
Judged accuracy of each prompt on the dev items.
questions.f: No judge ran, and no accuracy or H − Hc number was computed. The rule reads abstentions, gold presence and citation markers only.

o: The retrieval arms R, H, H-collapsed and G; L has its own closed-book prompt.
Only R and H, because the dev runs used them.
questions.f: P2 became the shared SYSTEM prompt of the retrieval arms. L answers from its own knowledge under its own prompt.

questions.q: Why must the prompt be fixed and hashed before the main run?
o: So no choice can respond to a main-set outcome: the prompt is part of what the test compares under.
Because a hashed prompt makes the model deterministic.
Because Claude needs a fixed prompt to run.
questions.f: A choice made after seeing results can drift toward a wanted outcome. Hashing it before the data it governs closes that path. Hashing does not make the model deterministic: that is why each answer is generated three times.
